s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral facial weakness with associated neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Slight slant of mouth corners towards left
Disappearance of nasolabial fold in right face
key_facts: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI
No hyper-intense signals in diffusion-weighted images
No vertebrobasilar artery main trunk occlusion or stenosis on MRTA
Significantly decreased amplitude of right facial nerve compound muscular action potential on ENoG
Presence of insertional activity in right facial muscles with greatly reduced voluntary activity on EMG

shortlist.label: Pontine glioma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive unilateral facial weakness with associated neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Brainstem glioma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI and progressive neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral facial weakness and associated neurological symptoms such as diplopia and hearing loss

shortlist.label: Stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden worsening of symptoms and lesion location in the brainstem

raw.rationale: The lesion located in the dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI, along with the hypo-intense signal in T1-weighted images and moderate-intense signal in T2-weighted images, is consistent with a brainstem glioma. The patient's symptoms, including facial muscle weakness, diplopia, and hearing loss, also align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pontine glioma
rejected.why: While similar, pontine glioma is more specific to the pons, and the lesion's location in the dorsolateral right pons could still be part of the brainstem, making brainstem glioma a broader and more encompassing diagnosis.

rejected.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: The significantly decreased amplitude of the right facial nerve compound muscular action potential and the presence of insertional activity in right facial muscles could suggest a facial nerve issue, but the lesion's location and MRI characteristics are more indicative of a brainstem glioma.

rejected.label: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome typically presents with a rash and is caused by varicella-zoster virus reactivation, which is not mentioned in the vignette. The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not align with Ramsay Hunt syndrome.

rejected.label: Stroke
rejected.why: The absence of hyper-intense signals in diffusion-weighted images and no vertebrobasilar artery main trunk occlusion or stenosis on MRTA make an acute stroke less likely. The gradual worsening of symptoms over 7 months also does not fit the typical acute onset of a stroke.

rejected.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not specifically support a diagnosis of facial nerve schwannoma, especially given the lesion's location in the brainstem and the broader range of symptoms beyond just facial nerve involvement.

gold: Right peripheral-type facial palsy due to dorsolateral pontine infarction
